Business Model Development

#Unit 3 — Business Model Development / Business Plan

Lecture hours 10
Marks carried in model question 12 — one 2-marker (A5 Business Model Canvas), case sub-part (c) "ensure benefit and trust to rider" (5 marks, draws on Unit 3 + 5), and C21(b) "essential elements of a business plan" (5 marks, half of C21)
Difficulty ★★☆☆☆ — pure memorisation. BMC 9 blocks, Business Plan 10 elements. Zero creativity needed.
Exam yield 🟡 standard — easy marks if memorised; lose them if vague
Prerequisite Unit 2 (validated idea + market → now build the model)
Syllabus bullets Business Model Canvas Framework · Identifying Revenue Sources · Cost Structure Analysis · Sustainability Business Models · Essential Elements of a Business Plan · Financial Projections Development · Marketing Strategy Formulation · Operational Planning Essentials · Risk Management Strategies · Case Study: Emerging Nepali tech startups

Read this first: this unit is the cheapest marks in the paper. A5 asks for BMC — draw the 9 blocks and name them. C21(b) asks for business plan elements — list the 10. The case part (c) asks for "benefit and trust to rider" — answer with BMC's value proposition + trust mechanisms (verified drivers, insurance, rating, fare transparency, support). Memorise the two lists and you secure 12 marks.

#3.1 Business Model Canvas (BMC) — the 9 blocks (A5)

The Business Model Canvas is a one-page framework that describes how a venture creates, delivers, and captures value — nine building blocks covering customers, offer, infrastructure, and financial viability.

#The 9 blocks (memorise in this order)

# Block Question it answers Nepal ride-share example
1 Customer Segments Who are we creating value for? Riders (commuters, students, tourists), Drivers (partners), Advertisers
2 Value Propositions What problem do we solve for each segment? Riders: safe, affordable, transparent rides. Drivers: flexible income, low commission.
3 Channels How do we reach and deliver to customers? Mobile app (iOS/Android), website, referral programme, corporate partnerships
4 Customer Relationships What relationship do we establish? Automated (app), self-service, 24/7 support, loyalty programme, safety features
5 Revenue Streams How do we make money? Commission per ride (15–20%), surge pricing, subscription (rider pass), ads
6 Key Resources What assets do we need? Platform (app + backend), driver network, brand, data, capital
7 Key Activities What do we do every day? Platform development, driver onboarding, safety ops, marketing, support
8 Key Partnerships Who helps us? Telecom (connectivity), payment gateways (eSewa/Khalti), insurance, regulators
9 Cost Structure What are our major costs? Platform dev, marketing, driver incentives, support, ops, legal/compliance

#A5 · "What is Business Model Canvas?" [2]

The Business Model Canvas is a one-page framework describing how a venture creates, delivers, and captures value through nine blocks: (1) Customer Segments — who we serve (riders, drivers, advertisers). (2) Value Propositions — problems solved (safe, affordable rides; flexible driver income). (3) Channels — how we reach users (app, web, referrals). (4) Customer Relationships — automated app, 24/7 support, loyalty. (5) Revenue Streams — commission (15–20%), surge, subscriptions, ads. (6) Key Resources — platform, driver network, brand, data. (7) Key Activities — dev, onboarding, safety, marketing. (8) Key Partnerships — telecom, payments, insurance. (9) Cost Structure — dev, marketing, incentives, ops.

(56 words. Definition + nine named blocks with one-line each.)

#3.2 Revenue sources and cost structure

#Identifying revenue sources (syllabus bullet)

Type Description Ride-share example
Transaction revenue per-use fee commission per ride
Recurring revenue subscription rider monthly pass, driver premium
Advertising revenue third-party ads in-app banners, partnered offers
Data/insights revenue aggregated, anonymised traffic patterns to city planners
Partnership revenue referral, affiliate insurance upsell, vehicle financing

#Cost structure analysis

Cost type Description Ride-share example
Fixed costs same regardless of volume platform dev, office, core team salaries
Variable costs scale with volume driver incentives, payment gateway fees, support
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) marketing + sales per new user referral bonuses, ads, promotions
Customer lifetime value (LTV) revenue per user over lifetime avg rides × commission × retention months

Key metric: LTV > 3× CAC for viable unit economics.

#3.3 Sustainability business models

Model Core logic Nepal example
Circular waste = resource e-waste recycling startup
Sharing economy access over ownership ride-share, tool library
Platform/ecosystem enable others to create value Khalti (payments platform)
Freemium free core, paid premium SaaS for Nepali SMEs
Social enterprise mission-first, profit-sustained Possible Health (rural telemedicine)

#3.4 Essential elements of a business plan (C21b)

A business plan is the detailed document that expands the BMC into an execution roadmap — used for internal alignment and external fundraising.

#The 10 essential elements (memorise this list for C21b)

# Element What it contains
1 Executive Summary one-page snapshot: problem, solution, market, team, ask
2 Company Overview mission, vision, legal structure, location, history
3 Problem & Solution the pain point, your product/service, why now
4 Market Analysis TAM/SAM/SOM, trends, target segments, competitive landscape
5 Business Model BMC expanded: revenue streams, pricing, unit economics
6 Marketing & Sales Strategy positioning, channels, funnel, CAC, retention, partnerships
7 Operational Plan team, hiring, processes, tech stack, suppliers, milestones
8 Financial Projections 3-year P&L, cash flow, balance sheet, assumptions, break-even
9 Risk Management key risks (market, tech, regulatory, team), mitigations
10 Funding Request / Appendix amount, use of funds, equity offered, cap table, supporting docs

#C21(b) · "What are the essential elements of a business plan?" [5]

The 10 essential elements: (1) Executive Summary — one-page snapshot (problem, solution, market, team, ask). (2) Company Overview — mission, vision, legal structure, location. (3) Problem & Solution — the pain point, your product, why now. (4) Market Analysis — TAM/SAM/SOM, trends, segments, competitors. (5) Business Model — BMC expanded: revenue, pricing, unit economics. (6) Marketing & Sales Strategy — positioning, channels, funnel, CAC, retention. (7) Operational Plan — team, hiring, processes, tech stack, milestones. (8) Financial Projections — 3-year P&L, cash flow, balance sheet, break-even. (9) Risk Management — key risks (market, tech, regulatory, team), mitigations. (10) Funding Request / Appendix — amount, use, equity, cap table, docs.

(56 words. Ten named elements, one-line each.)

#3.5 Financial projections (what to include)

Projection Horizon Key assumptions to state
Revenue model monthly, Year 1–3 rides/day, avg fare, commission %, take rate
Cost model monthly, Year 1–3 fixed (dev, salaries), variable (incentives, gateway fees), CAC
P&L monthly Y1, quarterly Y2–3 gross margin, EBITDA, net profit
Cash flow monthly Y1, quarterly Y2–3 operating, investing, financing; runway
Balance sheet Year 1–3 assets, liabilities, equity
Break-even month when cumulative cash flow turns positive
Unit economics per ride LTV, CAC, payback period, contribution margin

#3.6 Marketing strategy formulation (from BMC)

Component What to decide
Positioning "safe, affordable, transparent" vs "premium" vs "cheapest"
Target segments primary: Kathmandu professionals; secondary: students, tourists
Channels digital (FB/Google/Instagram), referral, corporate, PR
Funnel awareness → app install → first ride → repeat → advocate
Metrics CAC, install-to-ride rate, 30-day retention, NPS
Budget % of revenue, phased by channel performance

#3.7 Operational planning essentials

Area Decisions
Team founders, key hires (CTO, ops, safety, marketing), org chart
Processes driver onboarding, rider support, safety incident, payouts
Tech stack app (React Native/Flutter), backend (Node/Go), DB (PostgreSQL), infra (AWS/GCP)
Suppliers payment gateway, telecom, insurance, background check, vehicle partners
Milestones MVP launch, 1k rides/day, 10k rides/day, break-even, Series A

#3.8 Risk management strategies

Risk category Examples Mitigation
Market low adoption, competitor price war differentiated wedge, referral loop, brand
Technical app downtime, data breach multi-AZ, encryption, pen testing, IR plan
Regulatory permit denial, law change, labour dispute legal counsel, compliance calendar, driver contracts
Financial cash runway, fraud, payment disputes monthly forecasting, fraud detection, escrow
Team co-founder conflict, key hire loss vesting, clear roles, culture, retention bonuses

#3.9 Case sub-part (D22c) — "How do you ensure the benefit and trust to rider?" [5]

Shape: BMC value proposition + trust mechanisms (5 specific). ~150 words.

Ensuring rider benefit and trust in a Pathao-like ride-sharing app:

  1. Value proposition — safe, affordable, transparent rides (BMC Block 2): upfront fare, no surge surprise, ETA accuracy.
  2. Verified drivers — background check, licence verification, vehicle inspection, photo ID in app (BMC Block 7: safety ops).
  3. Insurance & SOS — trip insurance (partner with insurer), in-app SOS button sharing live location with contacts + police (BMC Block 4: safety relationship).
  4. Rating & accountability — two-way rating, driver deactivation for <4.0, rider refund for safety incidents (BMC Block 4: trust relationship).
  5. Fare transparency & support — upfront pricing, receipt with route map, 24/7 in-app chat support, 30-min dispute resolution (BMC Block 4: support relationship).

(156 words)

#3.11 Traps

Trap Why it costs marks Fix
Drawing BMC without all 9 blocks A5 asks "what is BMC" — 9 blocks = the answer memorise the 9 blocks in order with one-line each
Listing business plan elements without names C21b asks "essential elements" — 10 names = the answer memorise the 10 elements in order with one-line each
Case part (c) as generic "good service" must link to BMC blocks value prop (B2), verified drivers (B7), insurance/SOS (B4), rating (B4), fare transparency (B4)
Confusing revenue streams with pricing revenue stream = how money comes in; pricing = how much commission, surge, subscription, ads = streams
Missing LTV/CAC in cost structure unit economics is the viability test "LTV > 3× CAC" is the key metric

#3.12 Self-test (answers collapsed)

  1. Name the 9 blocks of the Business Model Canvas in order. (2 marks — A5)
  2. Give the ride-share example for each BMC block. (3 marks)
  3. List the 10 essential elements of a business plan. (5 marks — C21b)
  4. What are the 5 trust mechanisms for riders in a ride-sharing app? (5 marks — D22c)
  5. What is the difference between revenue stream and pricing? (2 marks)
  6. What is the key unit economics metric for viability? (2 marks)
Answers
  1. (1) Customer Segments, (2) Value Propositions, (3) Channels, (4) Customer Relationships, (5) Revenue Streams, (6) Key Resources, (7) Key Activities, (8) Key Partnerships, (9) Cost Structure.
  2. Segments: riders/drivers/advertisers. Value Props: safe rides / flexible income. Channels: app/web/referrals. Relationships: automated/24/7/loyalty. Revenue: commission/surge/subscription/ads. Resources: platform/driver network/brand/data. Activities: dev/onboarding/safety/marketing. Partnerships: telecom/payments/insurance. Costs: dev/marketing/incentives/ops.
    1. Executive Summary, 2. Company Overview, 3. Problem & Solution, 4. Market Analysis, 5. Business Model, 6. Marketing & Sales Strategy, 7. Operational Plan, 8. Financial Projections, 9. Risk Management, 10. Funding Request / Appendix.
  4. (1) Value prop: safe/affordable/transparent. (2) Verified drivers: background check, licence, vehicle inspection. (3) Insurance & SOS: trip insurance, SOS button. (4) Rating & accountability: two-way rating, deactivation, refunds. (5) Fare transparency & support: upfront pricing, receipt, 24/7 chat, 30-min dispute resolution.
  5. Revenue stream = how money comes in (commission, subscription, ads). Pricing = how much per unit (Rs. 15/km, 20% commission).
  6. LTV > 3× CAC (customer lifetime value > 3 times customer acquisition cost).
